messages:
Leah W: Heads-up from support: a customer copied our quickstart curl and got a 401 saying 'insufficient_scope' plus their Windows PowerShell quoting exploded.
Omar V: Can you paste exactly what they ran?
Leah W: From README under 'Make a request':
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-redwood-1\",\"input\":\"hey\"}'
```
Talia H: Two separate issues: (1) scoped keys now require the inference.write scope for POSTs and README doesn't mention it, (2) PowerShell users need double quotes and backticks or use --data-raw to avoid escaping pain. Also noticed sample-app config uses REDWOOD_KEY environment variable while README uses REDWOOD_API_KEY. Copy/paste mismatch.
Omar V: Reproduced locally by rotating a token during a run. After rotation the next request returned 401 + body `{\"error\":\"insufficient_scope\"}` with server log `auth: token present but missing scope: inference.write`.
Leah W: Proposed micro changes: (A) Insert a one-line 'Auth scopes' note above the curl: "POST requests require the inference.write scope; see Console -> API Keys." (B) Add a PowerShell-friendly curl example using double quotes and --data-raw, and a Windows CMD example. (C) Replace REDWOOD_KEY with REDWOOD_API_KEY across samples. (D) Add a small Ruby snippet showing use of retry middleware for parity with Node/Python. (E) Add a changelog at the top of README so support can point customers to the fix.
Talia H: For Ruby parity, here's a tiny example we can add under Advanced: ```ruby
# simple Faraday retry middleware example
require 'faraday'
conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.redwood.ai') do |f|
  f.request :retry, max: 4, interval: 0.5, backoff_factor: 2, exceptions: [Errno::ETIMEDOUT]
  f.adapter Faraday.default_adapter
end
resp = conn.post('/v1/generate', {model: 'gpt-redwood-1', input: 'hi'}.to_json, { 'Authorization' => "Bearer #{ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}", 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' })
```
Omar V: Also recommend adding a tiny docs linter in CI that scans sample repos for env var tokens (REDWOOD_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY) and flags mismatches. That will prevent copy/paste regressions.
Docs CI Bot: docs-ci: lint check failed on samples/sample-app/README.md (REDWOOD_KEY found). Opening PR suggestion.
Support Bot: support: tagging KB update request so support can reference troubleshooting steps for 'insufficient_scope' errors.
Leah W: I'll open a small PR to add the scope note, PowerShell + CMD examples, Ruby retry blurb, standardize env var names, and a changelog line: "2026-04-02: clarified auth scopes, fixed env var names, added PowerShell examples and retry guidance." Tagging @Talia H for snippet review.
Omar V: +1. Also add the CI linter job as a follow-up. Leaving thread open until PR merged. :thumbsup:
